title: UK's New Prime Minister Opens a Special Office in Manchester—and It's Not Just for Show!
summary: Imagine becoming the boss of a whole country—and then, in your very first week, you travel all over, talk to world leaders, and open a second office far from the capital! That's what Andy Burnham, the United Kingdom's new prime minister, did. He started Monday and hasn't slowed down. Burnham wants to spread power and money away from London to other parts of England. So on Friday, he opened "No. 10 North" in Manchester—a northern city about 260 kilometers from London. (The main office is at 10 Downing Street in London.) He called it "the nerve center for a rewired Britain." Some politicians say it's just a gimmick, but Burnham is serious. He wrote that for too long, decisions were made only in London, and struggling areas couldn't fix their problems. This week, he also made quick changes: a tax cut on home electricity bills, a £2 cap on bus fares (about $2.70), and a tax break for pubs. He said it's a "down payment" to show he understands people's struggles. Burnham faces big challenges, like a slow economy and frayed public services. He also has to deal with world problems. He told Ukraine's president that UK support is "resolute" and said Greenland's future should be decided by its people, not the US. Plus, Iran is angry because the UK lets US planes use British bases for airstrikes. Burnham's first week shows he's in a hurry to make changes—and he wants everyone to know it.
why_it_matters: Where decisions are made can affect everyday things like school budgets, bus fares, and electricity bills—so moving power to other cities could change your community.

background_read: The UK’s government has been based in London for centuries, but many people in other cities feel left out. Manchester is a big city in northern England that used to be a center of the Industrial Revolution.
A prime minister’s main office is at 10 Downing Street in London. Political leaders sometimes open extra offices in other regions to show they care about places far from the capital.
Article_Structure: WHO: Andy Burnham, the new prime minister of the United Kingdom
WHAT: Opened a second office called “No. 10 North” in Manchester
WHERE: Manchester, a northern city about 260 kilometers from London
WHY: To spread power and money away from London to other parts of England

perspectives.description: They believe moving government offices outside London helps spread jobs and attention to areas that often get ignored.
They argue the new office is a gimmick and won’t truly solve deep economic problems in struggling towns.
They may be excited that their city gets more attention, but wonder if it will lead to real changes.
